  ## The model (read first)
  
  The agent renders **generative UI inside the stage shell** — the model picks a
  screen and fills its data by calling a `Render<Component>` tool; the platform
  5: renders it as the stage's content (site mode) or inline in chat mode. The
  surface is the page's *content*, never the page — the shell owns the viewport,
  the scroll, and the chrome (see "Layout contract" below). You write a contract
  and a React component; the platform generates the tool from the contract, so a
  screen never needs a tool class of its own. (`createComponentTool` /
  `ComponentToolModel` are for channel-native embeds instead — see the discord
  integration skill.)
  throughout or it isn't.
  
  Builtins are for the screens nobody judges the look of: an internal tool, a
  utility, an admin or data view. Inside a branded agent a builtin is an exception
  you can justify — a dense table, a throwaway step — never the default you fall
  back to on the visitor's path. Either way the answer is a screen: neither a
  54: missing builtin nor a plain-looking one is a reason to fall back to prose.
  
  ## Free builtin catalog — know what it covers
  
  Every agent already ships a catalog of screens, rendered on the stage with no
  work from you. The catalog is `agent-dev-server/src/bl/builtin-catalog/` — one
  file per screen, each a `ComponentContract` whose `purpose` says what it is for
  file per screen, each a `ComponentContract` whose `purpose` says what it is for
  and whose `props`/`publishes`/`actions` are its exact shape. Read it before you
  design a screen: it is the source of truth, and it grows with the template. It
  is platform zone — read it, never edit it (client halves:
  `agent-dev-client/src/app/lib/a2ui/builtin-catalog/`).
